component.name: Stratagram
component.summary: Draw network diagrams that read the same for everyone

description.p: Stratagram is a network diagram editor for getting a network onto the screen in minutes. Standardized stencils and line types do the styling for you, so you think about the topology, and everyone on your team reads the result the same way.

ul.li: 28 device types with their own shapes, and line types with a meaning: 802.1Q trunk, L2, L3, IPsec, VXLAN, CAPWAP, SD-WAN, MPLS
Quick add: type “firewall, router, switch” and they appear, connected by auto layout
Front panels of switches, routers, firewalls, servers and patch panels, with cabling followed end to end
Layers, sheets, frames with title blocks and legends, light, dark and neon themes
Export to SVG, PNG, draw.io and Cisco Modeling Labs; draw.io import
Plain JSON files, and a command line to lay out and export diagrams from scripts

description.p: The same editor runs in the browser and inside NetBox, as a plugin that draws every site from NetBox's data.

screenshot.caption: A site drawn with Stratagram's stencils and line types
Front panels with numbered ports, cabled through patch panels
Device types, from switches and firewalls to clouds

description.p: A prebuilt Linux download with each release, and the AUR package stratagram-bin, which installs it without compiling.
A package for Arch Linux in the Arch User Repository. The app now identifies itself as app.stratagram.Stratagram, so desktops show its icon for its window.
Security: frame logos only from inside the diagram file, so opening a diagram never contacts another server.
Windows installer; .stratagram files open with Stratagram on Windows and Linux.
